problems.source_says: The validation study reports random selection of a thread and four comments for each annotator, with stance matching and random stance selection for neutral annotators. It does not explicitly establish that each annotator received both logical and dialectical conditions, or that their order was randomized. Thus the within-person designation is not explicitly supported; random stimulus selection itself is supported. This concerns a preparatory annotation study that the form already distinguishes from AI-assisted writing, so it does not overturn S4 eligibility.
problems.quote: Then, we showed them either one randomly selected homophobic or Islamophobic thread, along with four randomly selected LLM-generated comments written for that thread.
problems.locator: PDF pp. 7-8 (printed 410:7-410:8), Section 3.1, Validating Argumentation Style; no further specification in Appendix A, pp. 30-33.

confirmed.statement: S4 explicitly assigns individual participants randomly to control or test in a between-subjects writing experiment.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 10 (410:10), Section 3.2, Writing Task, first sentence; corroborated in the Introduction, pp. 2-3.

confirmed.statement: S4 control participants were instructed to write their own comments without external assistance, including the Internet or ChatGPT; this matches the no-AI comparison arm.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 10 (410:10), Section 3.2, paragraph beginning In the control group.

confirmed.statement: S4 test participants used the explicitly named LLM GPT-4 to rewrite their own initial drafts in real time, confirming generative-AI refinement assistance during production.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 10-11 (410:10-410:11), Section 3.2, test-group instructions, Figure 2 caption, and live rewriting prompt.

confirmed.statement: S4 required a draft of at least 20 words and at least one LLM request; participants could select or write prompts and accept, reject, regenerate, or edit suggestions before submission.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 11 (410:11), Figure 2 caption and Section 3.2, paragraphs following the prompt list.

confirmed.statement: S4 randomized thread order and prompt-list order; its initial-versus-final draft comparison is an additional before/after analysis within the test group, not a randomized crossover of assistance conditions.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 10, Writing Task; p. 11, paragraph beginning We randomized the order of the prompts; p. 12, Quantitative Analysis.

confirmed.statement: S1 randomizes stimulus selection for annotators who classify GPT-4 comments by argumentation style; it does not assign assistance for participants to produce their own writing.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 7-8 (410:7-410:8), Section 3.1, Validating Argumentation Style; p. 31, Table 12, GPT-4 stimulus-generation prompts.

confirmed.statement: S3 presents each participant with logical-versus-dialectical GPT-4 comment pairs and explicitly randomizes comment order within each pair; participants evaluate existing outputs rather than receive writing assistance.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 9-10 (410:9-410:10), Section 3.1, Experiment 1: Capturing Perceptions of Constructiveness.

confirmed.statement: S5 uses separate evaluators, randomly selected threads and comment pairs, and explicitly randomized comment order within pairs; these assignments concern evaluation stimuli.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 12 (410:12), Section 3.2, Human Evaluation of Constructiveness.

confirmed.statement: S5 compares existing control-group human comments, test-group human-AI comments, and Phase 1 LLM-generated comments; its AI-only versus human-only comparison is an output benchmark, not another randomized assistance experiment.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 12 (410:12), Section 3.2, Human Evaluation of Constructiveness, opening paragraph and list of pair types.

confirmed.statement: The appendix documents GPT-4 settings and prompts for generating Phase 1 stimuli; it supplies no additional assignment or condition-order procedure for the validation study.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 30-33 (410:30-410:33), Appendix A, Model Hyper-parameters and Tables 11-20.

summary: S4 explicitly randomizes writers to GPT-4 revision assistance or independent writing without external assistance, so criterion 1 holds. S1 has one unsupported detail: its within-person designation lacks explicit confirmation of exposure to both argumentation styles or randomized condition order.
